subject: Chronos: request for per-customer priority lanes and throttling (Q4 close ask)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Chronos: request for per-customer priority lanes and throttling (Q4 close ask)

Team —

Quick context: Chronos Analytics (large enterprise prospect, deal CH-2026-4273) is asking for a mechanism to guarantee sub-200ms median latency for a subset of critical tenants during peak hours. Their use case is time-series anomaly detection where certain customers pay for a guaranteed priority tier. They want a configurable per-customer "priority lane" that can be enforced across our hosted API and Dedicated deployments: essentially weighted request queues, preemptive throttles, and a soft-reservation feature so their high-tier tenants never see more than X% tail-latency degradation during spikes.

They expect this capability to be available in our product before contract signature; the procurement timeline is tight and Ben estimates a firm close target of 2026-11-30 if we can commit to a delivery window and SLO language in the SOW. Attached is Chronos' requirements doc and an updated SOW draft.

Asks:
- Product: can you surface a high-level implementation approach, tradeoffs, and an estimate (weeks) for a minimum viable capability that covers: 1) per-tenant priority labels, 2) request weighting/preemptive throttles, and 3) observability (per-tenant latency and utilization metrics)?
- Eng: rough resource estimate (engineering + infra), and any blockers for November delivery (regulatory, infra refactor, or major runtime changes).

If this is feasible, Ben will pitch the capability as a commercial feature in exec negotiation and we can lock the deal this month. If not feasible, we need a clear alternative (e.g. managed capacity lanes invoiced separately) that we can offer in SOW.

I'll coordinate a 30-min sync with Product + Eng this week if useful.

Thanks — Rafa

--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Chronos: request for per-customer priority lanes and throttling (Q4 close ask)

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear ask and attachments. I've read the Chronos doc; this looks like a prioritized QoS feature that sits between routing/policy and the serving runtime. High level reaction:

- Product POV: We can scope a "Priority Lane" MVP that implements tenant labels + request weighting in the smart routing layer, with runtime backpressure signals to avoid breaking the general SLOs. Observability would be surfaced via per-tenant dashboards and alerting.
- Tradeoffs: True hard-reservations (strict capacity pinning) will require changes to autoscaling and Dedicated pool planning — higher complexity and cost. MVP should be softer (priority queues + preemptive throttles + SLA reporting).
- Timeline: With a small team and one sprint of dedicated infra work + one sprint of runtime integration + another sprint for dashboards/QA, I estimate 6-8 weeks to a conservative MVP. That misses Ben's 11/30 target.

Next steps I suggest: 1) Dev, can you confirm if we can compress the infra + runtime work into 3 sprints with a small focused "deal squad"? 2) Rafael/Ben, if we can't hit 11/30, is Chronos willing to accept a phased approach: commit to feature design and a pilot (GA timeline TBD) and offer a commercial mitigation (discount or reserved capacity) up front?

I'm available for a quick triage call today 2–3pm PT.

—Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Chronos: request for per-customer priority lanes and throttling (Q4 close ask)

Marissa / Rafa —

Technical notes from Eng:

- Implementation idea (MVP): label requests with a per-customer priority field at the API gateway. Routing layer maintains separate small priority queues per priority class and applies weighted round-robin when dispatching to workers. Add soft preemption: mid-size requests from non-priority tenants can be deprioritized when priority queue length > threshold.
- Observability: emit per-tenant token-bucket metrics + latency histograms keyed by tenant_id and priority_class. This part is straightforward using our current telemetry stack, though retention and cardinality will increase cost.
- Major blockers: if Chronos expects guaranteed absolute latency percentiles (hard SLO backed by credits), we need either dedicated capacity reservations or kernel-level priority changes in the runtime (significant work). Soft-priorities + alerts is doable quickly.
- Estimate: With 2 backend engineers + 1 infra engineer + 1 QA, 3 sprints (~6 weeks) for a soft-priority MVP. To hit 3 sprints in 4 weeks we'd need to deprioritize other work and pull an on-call rotation; doable but risky.

Questions:
1) Chronos: do you need hard guarantees in the contract, or would a "priority lane with commitment to pilot and SLO monitoring" work for signing?
2) Sales: is there flexibility to price managed reserved lanes if we can't deliver hard guarantees by the close?

I'll sketch a minimal design doc and share this afternoon.

- Dev

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@chronos.ai>, Chronos Procurement <procurement@chronos.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Chronos: request for per-customer priority lanes and throttling (Q4 close ask)

Aisha / Procurement —

Thanks for the patience while we scoped the ask. Quick update and proposed path forward:

1) Product + Eng can deliver a soft-priority "Priority Lane" MVP that includes tenant labels, priority-weighted queues, soft preemption rules, and per-tenant telemetry. Estimate: 6 weeks from kickoff.
2) We cannot, without significant infra and runtime changes, deliver hard, contract-backed absolute latency guarantees by 11/30. To keep the deal moving, we're offering two commercial options:
   - Option A (Pilot + SOW): Commit to Priority Lane MVP + a 3-month pilot with weekly observability reviews and a roadmap to hard-reservations. We will add a pilot SLA for uptime and basic latency monitoring; no absolute tail latency credits. SOW attached.
   - Option B (Reserved Lanes): Provide dedicated capacity lanes for Chronos' high-tier tenant group at an additional monthly fee (this gives stronger practical isolation but is functionally separate from the routing-level priority work).

Ben and I can walk through the options in a short call. If Chronos is willing to accept Option A and sign the SOW for pilot + roadmap, we can keep the 11/30 commercial close intact and start engineering work immediately post-signature.

Next steps: 
- Aisha: indicate preferred option by 11/24 so we can finalize SOW and DocuSign.
- Marissa/Dev: if Option A, propose a compressed 6-week kickoff plan and a short-term headcount commitment for the deal squad.
- Hannah: prepare CS onboarding notes for a pilot and define success criteria for the three-month pilot.

Appreciate the team's quick triage on this.

Rafa

--
